vocab.title: Match each term to its meaning
defs: b
an employee identified as able to grow two levels or more
c
the group of people being prepared for future roles
d
a task deliberately above somebody current level, given to develop them
e
teaching the people you already employ new skills instead of hiring
f
how close somebody is to being able to do the next role
g
how many capable replacements a company has for its key roles
h
the sequence of roles somebody can move through inside a company
i
to prepare somebody deliberately for a particular role
j
to replace somebody who has left or moved, in the same role
a
a plan naming who could take a role if the person in it left

paras: This review covers the nine roles the leadership team has agreed are critical in Brazil. For each one it names a successor, grades their readiness as now, one year or two years, and says what is missing. It does not use the word maybe. A role with no name against it is written as having no name against it, because that is information and a vague name is not.

Four of the nine have a successor graded as ready now. Three have a successor at one year. Two have nobody, and both of those are in engineering, where we have been trying to build a pipeline for two years without success. That is the headline of this review and it has not changed since last year, which is itself the finding.

One case deserves attention. Ana has been with the company for eleven years and has been running the São Paulo site since March. She has rebuilt onboarding and has taken two supervisors up to shift manager. She has been graded as ready for two years running and has not moved, because the role above her has not become vacant. She has not complained. People in that position rarely complain and frequently leave.

What we have been doing and what we have not. We have trained forty people through external programmes and we have promoted four of them, which is a return nobody would accept on any other line of the budget. What we have not been doing is giving people jobs slightly too big for them. The recommendation of this review is to move the development budget from courses to stretch assignments, and to count, for the first time, the roles we will have to backfill each time somebody moves up.
reading.source: Alumni by Better -- succession review written for this lesson, with all names and figures invented

choices: That the succession plan is complete and the pipeline is healthy.
That the development money is going to the wrong kind of development, and the gaps have not moved in a year.
That two engineering roles should be filled externally as soon as possible.

items: A critical role with no successor is left blank rather than filled with a vague name.
The note says a role with no name against it is written as having no name against it, because that is information and a vague name is not.

The note says it has not changed since last year, which is itself the finding.

The note says she has been graded ready for two years running and has not moved, because the role above her has not become vacant.

items.situation: Ana joined eleven years ago and is still here. Say it.
tips: She has been with us for eleven years.
Never the present simple for duration up to now.

items.situation: The programme started in March and is still running. Say it.
tips: We have been running the programme since March.
Since for the starting point, for for the length.

items.situation: Forty trained, four promoted. Say both in one sentence.
tips: We have trained forty people and we have promoted four of them.
Results, so the simple present perfect.

items.situation: Ask a colleague how long they have been considering a move.
tips: How long have you been thinking about that move?
Inversion in the question, and the continuous for the ongoing thought.

items.situation: Grade somebody readiness without using the word maybe.
tips: I would grade her readiness at one year, and what is missing is finance exposure.
A grade and a gap. Never maybe.

items.situation: Say what a promotion creates that nobody counts.
tips: Every promotion creates a role to backfill.

listenings.text: I have been doing this for nineteen years and I can tell you where the money goes. It goes to courses, and courses are the least effective development there is, and everybody in this room already knows that. What actually moves somebody is a job that is slightly too big for them, with somebody watching. That is it. That is the whole science. A stretch assignment costs nothing and works, and a course costs four thousand dollars and produces a certificate. So why do we keep buying courses? Because a course is easy to approve and a stretch assignment requires a manager to accept some risk on their own numbers. Nobody wants to be the manager whose project went wrong because they gave it to somebody who was not quite ready. Until we solve that, we will keep spending the budget on rooms with slides in them.

I have been running plants for twelve years and I got the first one because somebody took a risk that, honestly, I would probably not take today. I had been a supervisor for two years. Two. There were people on that site who had been there longer than I had been alive, and I was going to tell them how to run a shift. What made it work was not me. It was that my director told me, in front of nobody, that he expected me to get about a third of it wrong and that his job was to catch the third that mattered. He had been doing this long enough to know which third that was. And he checked in every Friday for six months, twenty minutes, never longer. I have given three people that same jump since then, and I have not always got it right, but not once has the problem been that they were not ready. It has been that I was not watching.
